Hi all! I tend to work on converting board games into digital, touch-screen applications. I'm currently working on converting a game called Pixel Glory.

All of my games play on a table with an inlaid TV and a multi-touch overlay. This game is slightly different from my other games because I'm making modes to make the game playable from a vertically-oriented TV. It also requires players to connect via HTTP to the game to control their wizards.

I hope to post more over the following weeks, but here's a screen capture of the dungeon mode.
Looks great! How do you play it?

Thanks!

Players play as wizards. First, they visit town and purchase spells using an auction system. After everybody has 9 spells (and a few basic attacks), they visit the dungeon where they hunt down 13 creatures using a deck management system.

The town only awards glory for the killing blow, so the wizards must be careful. While a wizard must play every card in his hand in an appearance at helping, he doesn't have to make it easier for the next player to get a kill.

There are some differences between the board game and my version. My version supports 6 players (up from 4). This would normally create too much downtime between players, but I also support a mode called "Wandering Monsters" or "The Multiverse". Logically, I'm creating as many copies of the dungeon as there are players and players rotate between the copies. Thematically, players are in rooms and the monsters wander between rooms after each turn.
Seems like a intensive game in terms of memory. Does the player load up all dungeon copies in the beginning or when they switch to them?

The bulk of the action takes place on one screen/one computer. "Wandering Monsters" does load all of the dungeons simultaneously and displays them all on the screen, but the vast majority of the graphics are made up of lightweight quads. The internal model of the dungeon itself is kept separate and comes in under 50 kilobytes, so cloning isn't much of an issue.
